transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… thanks. I guess I’m here because it’s gotten really bad at work, and I don’t really know how to keep pretending it’s fine anymore.

I’m a barber, and the straight razor has become this whole… problem for me. Like, I’ll do almost anything to avoid having to use it. I’ll switch clients with someone if I can, or I’ll make some excuse like the blade’s missing, or I’ll literally hide it in the drawer so I don’t have to pick it up. And I know that sounds ridiculous because it’s part of the job, but in the moment it feels like I just need to get away from it.

And if I can’t avoid it—like if I’m stuck doing a shave—I’m shaking through the whole thing. I’m trying to look normal and keep my hand steady, but inside I’m just tense the entire time. It’s embarrassing, honestly.
When you have to use the straight razor, are you mainly afraid that you might accidentally cut or seriously hurt the client?

Yeah. That’s pretty much the center of it, I think. It’s not like I don’t understand what it is — I mean, I trained with straight razors, I know how they work, and I can use clippers or scissors all day without thinking twice. But when the straight razor is open and sitting there at my station, it suddenly feels completely different.

It’s like my brain just locks onto the edge of it, and all I can think is, what if my hand slips, what if I cut the client, what if I do something really bad before I can stop it. And sometimes it’s also about me, like I’ll picture cutting myself badly too. I know that probably sounds dramatic, because it’s just a tool and I’m supposed to be comfortable with it, but in that moment it feels like I’m holding something dangerous and I’m about to hurt somebody or hurt myself.
When you’re holding the straight razor, do you ever get a sudden unwanted thought or urge that you might intentionally slash or stab the client?

I don’t know if I’d put it that way. Like… “intentionally” sounds different from what it feels like for me.

When I’m holding it, I’m not sitting there wanting to slash someone or planning to do anything like that. It’s more like this sudden panic about the fact that I *could* hurt them because the razor is sharp and it’s right there in my hand. My mind kind of jumps to a bad image or a “what if” scenario, like what if something goes wrong, what if my hand moves wrong, what if I lose control somehow. But it doesn’t feel like an urge where I want to do it.

Honestly, even saying it out loud makes me feel awful, because I don’t want anyone thinking I’d actually hurt a client. That’s the whole reason it scares me so much. I’m trying so hard not to hurt anybody. So… no, I don’t think it’s an urge to intentionally slash or stab someone. It’s more fear that something terrible could happen while I’m holding it.
Do you find yourself doing any repeated ritual or checking with the straight razor to feel safer?

Um… rituals? I don’t think so. Not in the way I imagine you mean, like doing a certain thing over and over until it feels “right” or anything.

I mean, I’ll look at it, and I’ll be very aware of where it is, and sometimes I’ll kind of make sure it’s closed or put away because I don’t want it just sitting there open. But I don’t think I have, like, a repeated routine with it. It’s more that I avoid touching it if I can, or I try to get through it as fast and carefully as possible if I absolutely have to use it.

I might check that the blade is secure or that I’m holding it properly, but honestly that feels more like normal barber stuff, or me trying not to make a mistake, not some specific ritual I have to do a certain number of times. I don’t count or repeat phrases or anything like that. I mostly just feel tense and want it out of my hand.
Outside of work, do you also feel this kind of fear around other knives or sharp objects?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I don’t think I react the same way to every sharp thing, if that’s what you mean. Like, if I’m at home and there’s a kitchen knife on the counter, I don’t usually have that same immediate locked-up feeling that I get with the straight razor at work.

But I guess I do notice sharp objects more than some people might. If I’m using a knife to cook, I’m careful, maybe overly careful, but it doesn’t usually take over my whole body the same way. With the straight razor, it’s like everything narrows down to that edge and the person sitting in the chair, and there’s this pressure because it’s right near someone’s skin and face or neck. That’s the part that makes it feel different.

So… outside of work, no, not really in the same intense way. I wouldn’t say I’m comfortable with sharp things exactly, but I also don’t avoid all knives or anything like that. It’s mostly that specific situation with the razor.
When you are not around the straight razor or in a shaving situation, do you ever have sudden panic attacks out of the blue?

Not really… I mean, I’m trying to think if there are times where panic just hits me for no reason, like sitting at home or walking around or whatever, and I don’t think that’s really what happens.

When I get that intense panicky feeling, it’s usually tied to the razor or to being in that shaving situation, like having it in my hand or knowing I’m about to have to use it. If I’m away from that, I can still think about it and get uncomfortable, but I wouldn’t say I have these sudden attacks completely out of nowhere.

I guess sometimes I feel tense before work or if I know I’m scheduled for clients where I might have to shave someone, but even then it’s connected to that. It’s not like I’m just watching TV and suddenly my heart is racing for no reason. At least, I haven’t really noticed that.
Aside from the straight razor situation, do you spend a lot of time worrying about many other parts of your life?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in the way you’re describing, like worrying about everything all the time. I mean, I have normal stress, I guess — bills, work being busy, whether I’m doing a good job, family stuff sometimes — but it doesn’t feel like my whole life is one big list of worries.

The straight razor thing is different. That’s the one that really takes up space in my head. I can think about other things and get stressed like anyone, but I don’t usually sit there for hours worrying about every possible bad thing in my life. It’s more like if something connects back to shaving or using the razor, then my mind gets stuck on it.

So… aside from that, no, I wouldn’t say I spend a lot of time worrying about many different areas. At least I haven’t noticed that about myself.
